extraction_notes: Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and Fig. 3 contain usable plots. Forward, reverse, and capacitance curve points were directly digitized from the plotted curves; no intermediate points were synthesized. Plot current values were converted from the displayed mA or uA axes to A, and plot capacitance values were converted from pF to F.

Fig. 1 shows typical instantaneous forward characteristics at Ta = 25 degC and Ta = 100 degC. Fig. 2 shows typical reverse-current magnitude at Ta = 25 degC and Ta = 100 degC. The reverse-current curves are represented as positive magnitudes because the graph plots reverse current magnitude.
Fig. 3 shows typical junction capacitance between terminals at Ta = 25 degC and f = 1 MHz. The tabulated capacitance is a maximum of 2.0 pF at VR = 0 V and f = 1.0 MHz.

Absolute maximum ratings from p. 1 at Ta = 25 degC include VRRM = 70 V, VRMS = 70 V, VDC = 70 V, IF(AV) = 70 mA, IFSM = 100 mA for an 8.3 ms half-sine wave, PD = 200 mW, and Tj = -55 to +150 degC. VRRM/VDC are operating limits, not published breakdown-voltage or breakdown-current data; breakdown_voltage and breakdown_current are therefore null.

The electrical-characteristics table publishes maximum forward voltage at IF = 1 mA and 15 mA, maximum reverse current at VR = 50 V, maximum terminal capacitance at VR = 0 V and f = 1 MHz, and maximum reverse recovery time at IF = IR = 10 mA and RL = 100 ohm.
